narrative:
The model determined that you have a 48% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability is high enough to cross the bank's approval threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were the status of your checking account, the amount you requested, and the length of time you have been employed. Your checking account status had the largest impact and pushed the decision toward denial. Having a balance below zero is relatively uncommon among approved applicants (only 12.6% of them show a negative balance), and the model sees this as a clear warning sign of higher risk. 

The loan amount you requested worked in your favor. At 2,406 DM it is noticeably below the average requested by approved borrowers (3,020 DM), which helped reduce the predicted risk. Similarly, your 4–7 years of continuous employment also pulled the prediction toward approval; this is a stable employment period that the model generally views positively compared with shorter tenures.

Unfortunately, the negative influence from your checking account outweighed these positive signals. 

You should focus on clearing your checking account into positive territory and, if possible, wait until you have built a stronger positive balance before re-applying. This single change is likely to have the biggest effect on future decisions.
